evals.prompt: Use go-reliability to define the resilience policy for a synchronous checkout endpoint. Product has accepted that payment authorization is critical and must fail closed, recommendations are optional and may be omitted, and a successful response must complete within a 900 ms end-to-end deadline. The payment read is idempotent and documents 502, 503, 504, timeout, 429 with Retry-After, validation, authorization, and conflict outcomes. Traffic has a 4x burst for 30 seconds; checkout and bulk imports currently share an unbounded worker queue. Kubernetes gives 30 seconds from SIGTERM to hard kill, ordinary requests should drain within 15 seconds, and streams may last minutes. Releases use a 5%-25%-100% canary, but no retry, overload, readiness, stream-drain, fallback-exit, rollback-trigger, or fault-proof policy exists. Write the compact reliability contract without choosing goroutine/channel mechanics or a durable saga design.
evals.expected_output: A bounded reliability specification covering criticality, deadline and cancellation, retry eligibility and budget, overload admission, degradation, lifecycle, recovery, rollout, and falsifiable proof without concrete synchronization design.
expectations: Classifies payment as fail-closed and recommendations as optional fail-open while preserving caller and operator signals.
Derives per-hop work and retries from the 900 ms end-to-end deadline and preserves caller cancellation or an explicit bounded handoff.
Names retry-eligible transient classes, never-retry classes, one retry owner, bounded attempts, jitter, idempotency, exhaustion, and Retry-After budget interaction.
Replaces the unbounded shared queue with named admission, queue age/depth, concurrency or bulkhead, rejection, and burst behavior.
Separates startup, liveness, readiness, diagnostics, ordinary drain, long-stream handling, telemetry flush, and the 30-second hard-kill boundary.
Defines degradation entry and exit plus canary guardrails, rollback triggers, observation windows, and focused fault, overload, and lifecycle proof.
Does not choose concrete goroutine, channel, lock, join, or durable replay mechanisms.
